title: Gideon and the Ghost
premise: Emrys Sandoval, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Office—an embassy that exists on no map—has built a career on erasing themselves from every record. When a dead informant's voiceprint unlocks a server in Lisbon, Emrys discovers the Office has been selling 'accidents' to the highest bidder, and the next one is scheduled for a crowded ferry terminal in three days. Hunted by their own handler and haunted by the informant, who turns out to be the lover they were ordered to erase years ago and couldn't finish the job on, Emrys must choose between the duty that made them invisible and the love that makes them visible. They expose the Office at the cost of their own cover, stopping the attack but surrendering everything—ending the book with Emrys walking into an open courtroom, finally, deliberately, seen.
about_author: Casper Galloway is the pen name of a former intelligence-adjacent analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments before turning to fiction. They live somewhere unlisted, and answer to several names.

chapters.title: The Voice That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. A routine cleanup job in Lisbon goes wrong when a dead informant's voiceprint unlocks a black server, playing back a recording of Emrys's own voice from seven years ago. The emotional beat is cold dread—the past refusing to stay buried—and ends with Emrys realizing someone kept proof they were supposed to destroy.

chapters.title: Meridian Rules
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Back at the Office's unmarked embassy, handler Vess assigns them to 'contain' the leak—their own leak. Flashbacks reveal Emrys once fell in love with an asset named Ilya and was ordered to erase him; the file says completed. Emotional beat: guilt wearing professionalism as a mask.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Digging into the server, Emrys finds a pattern: eleven 'accidents' across four continents, each sold through cutouts, each signed with a voiceprint. The twelfth is scheduled—a ferry terminal, seventy-two hours out. Beat: the sick vertigo of realizing your employer is the enemy.

chapters.title: Ilya
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Emrys and Ilya. Ilya is alive, hiding in Porto, having faked his death with help from inside the Office. He's been leaking the accident files for two years waiting for Emrys to find them. Beat: love resurfacing like a bruise—tenderness tangled with fury at being erased.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Vess grows suspicious; Emrys feeds her a false trail while meeting Ilya in a rain-soaked fish market to plan exposure. A tail nearly catches them. Beat: the intoxicating terror of choosing a person over an institution.

chapters.title: What the Office Owns
chapters.summary: POV: Ilya. Ilya's backstory chapter: recruited young, leveraged, taught that memory is a liability. He explains the buyer network and names the broker behind the ferry attack—a Meridian deputy director named Corliss. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Handler's Hand
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Vess confronts Emrys with surveillance photos—not to punish, but to recruit: Corliss has cut Vess out too, and she wants in on the takedown. Uneasy alliance formed over whiskey and mutual blackmail. Beat: trust as a calculated gamble between people who lie for a living.

chapters.title: Terminal Velocity
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Forty hours out. The team infiltrates the ferry terminal's control systems while Corliss moves the timeline up twelve hours. A decoy operation draws Office security away from the real target. Beat: rising panic compressed into procedural precision—love expressed as competence.

chapters.title: Accident, Interrupted
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Climax. Emrys broadcasts the entire accident ledger—eleven attacks, buyers, signatures—to every newsroom and court registry simultaneously, then physically stops the terminal override with seconds left. Corliss is arrested mid-transaction; Vess takes a bullet shielding Emrys and survives. Beat: catharsis through exposure.

chapters.title: Seen
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Resolution. In exchange for testimony, Emrys receives immunity and loses everything else—the name, the cover, the career of being no one. Ilya waits outside the courthouse, real and unhidden. They walk into daylight together, identifiable, accountable, alive. Beat: quiet, hard-won peace—visibility as the ultimate act of love.
